name: Lord Maloquence
gmNotes:
To the many heretics of the Faithful Writ, Maolquence burns. He is a Dark Apostle, drawing fiends to him like moths to a flame. Through ritual and sacrifice, his sorcerers assist foul creatures in breaking through into realspace and possessing the bodies of his followers. From his power comes the name ‘Faithful of the Writ’, those followers who obey his every command as law.

But where was this terror spawned? None can be sure, Maloquence tells many varied tales of his own origins. In one version, he witnessed the Dropsite Massacre of Istvaan V. In another he claims to have been present when the Warmaster slew Sanguinius. Who knows? Perhaps even Maloquence himself isn’t sure.

Maloquence has served the Dark Gods with monstrous devotion for ten thousand years. He wears their boons and blessings upon both armour and flesh – jutting horns, weeping sores, leering eyes and fanged mouths all bearing foul testament to his favour.

Maloquence’s desires are not complicated — he simply wants to tear the Imperium to shreds and have a statue of himself made from the ashes of the empire that wronged him. It is not enough that the Imperium falls; the galaxy and the gods must know that it was Maloquence that made it so. Such mad ambition, especially from a leader sequestered within an asteroid in an isolated system, would normally be the object of scorn, but for all his madness Maloquence cuts an inspiring figure, and his zeal is enough to convince his followers he is capable of such lofty goals.

To succeed in the tasks he sets is to be exalted and eventually become one of the Faithful, eminent among the Writ. Some may even be gifted with possession by a daemon of the Empyrean.

To fail him is to be fodder for those who succeed.

To this end, he bends the Faithful Writ to a multitude of purposes. Some of his mightiest followers, the twisted Possessed and their Traitor Astartes brothers are his hammer, intended to smash foes in precision strikes before extracting back to the safety of the asteroid via archeotech teleporters and the foul touch of the Warp itself.

His mortal followers are used for much more insidious ends. Agents of the Faithful Writ masquerade on numerous worlds within Gilead as legitimate priests of the Ecclesiarchy, revering certain sacred texts that they claim were penned by Saint Julyanna herself. These texts are so convincing that many otherwise pious readers believe they are truly holy. This could not be further from the truth: they were scratched by Maloquence’s own hand, and subtly twist the minds of those who read them.

Maloquence desires only that the Imperium in Gilead falls, but cares not how it’s done. He will use anything he can get his foul claws on, be that archeotech, unwitting pawns within the Administratum of Gilead or simply the numerous mortals he can bend to his will and service.

name: Verit Maalazitor
role: Cult Demagogue, Disciples of the Ninth Eye Blinded
gmNotes:
The Disciples of the Ninth Eye Blinded aboard The Diver’s Bell are led by Verit Maalazitor, a Cult Demagogue of titanic strength and undeniable charm. Her face shrouded under a terrifying horned mask, clad in oil slicked robes, and carrying an enormous staff adorned in foul talismans and texts. The Cults exists in the darkest reaches of the ship, far from prying eyes. They attract only the most curious, who quickly turn into followers, whereupon they are lead to a dingy room deep in the bowels of the ship where they are initiated into the cult by means of traditional Bathysquid ink tattoos.

Verit is affected by seizures, which her followers believe are holy visions. The truth is that they are Astropathic missives sent by the Writ’s Psykers, instructing her to taint the ink with a ‘sacred unguent’ that arrives as part of the ship’s weekly deliveries. Verit will not tolerate interference from the pompous fools of the Ecclesiarchy or any who would take her away from her loyal cultists. She must be with them to protect and guide her flock as well as make sure the work is done. The voices whisper that unfaithful souls are aboard The Diver’s Bell, who would attempt to stop her sacred work, and any who interfere must be dealt with.

PLOT HOOK: TWISTED RATIONS
Adren Voss, a sailor on The Diver’s Bell, has stolen a package from the weekly supply shipment, a crate of Protien Haemo-Sausage, and has been using it to supplement his weekly ration. A lethal mistake — this chalky stuff is Possessed Astartes blood. Intended to taint the holy ink, it’s mutated Adren and the twisted sailor is now stalking the lower decks of the ship. The ship’s master, Lovjen Karaz, wants the mutant dealt with and the source of the infection discovered. Verit meanwhile wants the missing shipment found, for without it, her holy work cannot continue.

PLOT HOOK: PECULIAR THEFTS
The Diver’s Bell possesses a small Ministorum shrine of its own — known as ‘The Chapel of Architeuthis’s Blood’, it is tended by an aged and withered priest, Elspen Croy. Elspen is a faithful servant of the Emperor, diligent in her work, and has noticed that texts from the chapel library have started to go missing. Nothing overly important: a compendium of folktales about Old Nine Eyes, a primer on abyssal diving, an ancient esoteric prayer book. Elspen would like these books found, but more importantly, would like to know why these particular books were taken in the first place.

MASTER PLAN: OLD NINE EYES
Verit’s visions are getting more intense — every night her dreams are invaded by Old Nine Eyes, labouring up from the depths to spell doom for the The Diver’s Bell. With agents on the move, hunting for the mysterious recipient of the parcel, Verit knows she needs to do something to stop the tragedy, the voices urging her to take action and save the ship before she is captured. In reality, the Writ is directing Verit to summon Old Nine Eyes (in fact a Tzeentchian Screamer), hoping to harvest its “ink” for use in the ritual that will transform Maloquence into a daemon prince.

Research into the chapel’s books might direct the player characters towards figuring out the plans of the cult aboard The Diver’s Bell: summoning the legendary Nine Eyes via the submersible diver’s bell for which the ship is named, stockpiling it with the Possessed Astartes blood and using it as a lure to draw the colossal creature from its realm.

If the source of the blood is identified, or who it was intended to be delivered to, the cult might be exposed, enabling the player characters to strike and stop the ritual before it is commenced. Locating the conspirators is difficult though, as they are secreted away within the depths of the ship.

If the ritual begins, it starts on the diving bell platform located on the back of the ship. Gunfire erupts as the cult takes over the control bridge of the submersible, while some cultists carry the packets of tainted blood into the bell, and others paint the outside of the capsule in corrupted runes daubed in Bathysquid ink. Verit intends to descend in the diving bell alongside the Cult’s Mindwitch, a psychic beacon to draw the creature into realspace.

If Verit perishes, or the diving bell is somehow prevented from descending beneath the ocean waves, the cultists’ plans fail. The cell quickly falls apart: without Verit’s ‘divine’ direction they have no purpose, and many offer themselves to the churning waves.

If the diving bell descends, then all is lost. Old Nine Eyes emerges from the deep, a slimy manta-like leviathan, as wide as The Diver’s Bell itself. The water turns luminescent as it disgorges streams of multicoloured light in its wake, which servants of the Writ are standing by to scoop from the waters. The mission then becomes a race to escape The Diver’s Bell by any means possible, as the abyssal monstrosity begins to break the ship in two.

name: Massintos
role: Wielder of Fates, Summoner of the Writ
gmNotes:
While Massintos styles himself as ‘the Wielder of Fates’, a better title might be ‘the jealous’. Though a powerful summoner in his own right, Massintos’s power pales in comparison to Maloquence, who uses him to carry out mundane sorceries and alchemy as he requires. Massintos chafes at these tasks he sees as beneath him, and has started planning his own ascension to power, mainly by subverting Maloquence’s efforts to elevate himself to the position of daemon prince instead. He believes this will give him an opportunity to unseat his lord, as the other underlings rage at their master’s failure.

PLOT HOOK: VOICES IN THE STONE
Noctilith, otherwise known as Blackstone, is a Warp-reactive stone that can either amplify or dampen the effects of the Empyrean. Cogni-Alpha 6, a tech-priest dispatched to investigate odd readings within Daedalon’s labyrinth, has reason to believe there may be a deposit nearby as workers have been reporting numerous psychic disturbances, such as hearing voices and seeing ethereal shapes stalking the labyrinth. In reality, the Noctilith in question is a component of Massintos’s device, being transported through the tunnels by his slaves. Cogni-Alpha 6 would like the intrusion dealt with and the priceless Blackstone retrieved.

PLOT HOOK: THE CRASSUS HOLY TALLOW RECLAIMATORUM
In the Crassus Holy Tallow Reclaimatorum corpses are melted down and repuposed. The fat is used to make sacred votive candles for use in Ecclesiarchal ceremony. Bishop Godren accuses the Administratum presence of stealing candles to use as grease for their scribing machines, while Administratum delegates counter-claim that the priests are inept and that huge quantities of metal shipped to make candle holders are unaccounted for. Massintos’s servants are responsible for both thefts, using the metal in the construction of their arcane machine and using the fat as a component in making explosives, in order to make the charges that will collapse the labyrinth and expose the machine to the skies ready for teleportation.

MASTER PLAN: A RITUAL SUMMONING
Massintos’s plan is nearly ready: he is altering the machine so that instead of channelling the power of the Warp into Maloquence, it will instead be released wildly into the bodies of anyone standing in the vicinity, the crackling blue flames reducing them to gibbering piles of Tzeentch-pleasing sludge.

As the characters come to the manufactorum, Massintos is making the final alterations to the machine. He has ordered the demolition charges to be armed, and they are counting down to explode and reveal the device to the heavens and Maloquence’s summoning ritual. He is on a tight deadline: he needs to finish the alterations at the last minute so none of those around him faithful to Maloquence notice what he is doing and warn their lord. He orders the other sorcerers to attack the PCs as he works. If he is undisturbed and manages to complete his work, the ceiling will blow, exposing the machine, and the blinding flare of the arcane ritual will arrive a few seconds later, transporting the sabotaged machine to Brother’s Ruin.

If the characters successfully managed to retrieve or destroy the Noctilith that Massintos was shipping in to complete the device, Massintos has been forced to improvise, replacing it with a set of much less potent Psy-Dampers. This will spell disaster whether or not he manages to make the alterations, as unlike the stable Noctilith Warp anchors, the Psy-Dampers will not be able to contain the raw power of the Warp, simply causing the machine to malfunction and explode in a titanic blast.

If the PCs managed to stop the theft of the candle fat, the explosives are also incomplete, meaning that the manufcatorum’s interior cannot be exposed to the sky and the machine cannot be teleported out. Fearing Maloquence’s wrath should he fail to deliver the machine, Massintos and the other sorcerers attempt to move it with concentrated effort to funnel their sorcerous powers, blasting a hole through the roof to deliver the device to Maloquence. If this is necessary, Massintos has no time to make the alterations he desired, and the machine travels to Maloquence complete (or without the Noctilith, as the case may be). This course of action sees the other sorcerers drained to husks by the effort and Massintos seriously injured.

Whatever state the machine leaves in, Massintos will not go quietly: he attempts to escape at any cost, valuing his life over even sabotaging Maloquence. Injured, he may well tell all of Maloquence’s plan, in a desperate attempt to save his own skin, distracting Players long enough to make his escape. If his plan has succeeded, then he needs to be alive to take control of the Faithful Writ, and if he has failed, he must survive to once again attempt to unseat Maloquence another time.

name: Ara'vitu'urhal
gmNotes:
Accompanying Massintos everywhere is the daemon he has bound, Ara’vitu’urhal, shambling morosely behind its master. Its once vibrant pink flesh has taken on a sickly paleness and as it walks the panoply of mutated warp-slicked arms that have erupted from its flesh over time lifelessly drag behind it. When spoken to, its manner is one of constantly scraping and simpering to the great Massintos, Wielder of Fates.

In truth though, this is all an act. Massintos doesn’t know what he’s unleashed, and the daemon “Ara’vitu’urhal” is not what it seems.

Drawn to the grandiose scheme and plotting of both Massintos and Maloquence, taking the form of the daemon Massintos intended to summon to its ritual binding, The Changeling, one of Tzeentch’s most favoured, thoroughly enjoys the game it has found itself in. The Changeling can manifest itself elsewhere whenever it pleases. Can take the form of any being it encounters, from lowly hive scum to mighty Greater Daemons. It is even canny enough to leave a facsimile of its mind behind, able to perform the ridiculous triflings that Massintos demands of it.

The Changeling sees infinite potential for interference and amusement in the intrigues of Massintos and his mewling lord Maloquence. How then to best engineer these deceptions? It’s considered a variety of creative and ironic schemes. Knowing that Massintos secretly fears possession, perhaps the device he is working on could redirect the energies of the Warp into its creator? Or maybe it could be modified to turn all those nearby into gibbering Spawn. It could even simply explode, tearing a fresh Warp rift in realspace, allowing Maloquence to be devoured by the daemons he covets so much.

The Changeling approaches the characters directly: it knows they could be powerful tools in subverting the plans of Massintos and Maloquence both. Whether it comes in disguise as a faithful Imperial servant or as whispered dream missives is up to you, but always remember, as a servant of Tzeentch, The Changeling is definitely playing every side for fools.

PLOT HOOK: A BLOOD-STAINED INVITATION
A mysterious missive arrives for the characters. It may take the form of an official Administratum request, to investigate errors in the components tally in Daedalon’s labyrinth. If the group contains a Psyker, they may be visited in the dead of night by haunting visions. It may even simply be a grimy note with ‘DAEDALON’S LABYRINTH’ scrawled on it in fresh blood.

Whatever the case, The Changeling is directing the characters to investigate the oddities of Daedalon’s labyrinth, hoping that they will stumble upon Massintos’s plans, infuriating its ‘master’ for its own amusement.

PLOT HOOK: THE PRIEST IN THE DARKNESS
The more the PCs curtail Massintos’s plans, the more gleeful The Changeling becomes. The daemon delights in watching its master vexed and if the PCs can frustrate the sorcerer enough, the daemon will find itself compelled to seek them out for one final act. Appearing as a blind Ministorum Preacher, the PCs encounter The Changeling in the labyrinth, and it offers up information on Massintos’s plans and how to stop them: the machine has a master power inductor and pulling that out will prevent it from being activated. This is a half-truth: it will stop the power being channelled into Maloquence, instead allowing it to spew out and create a Warp gate.

name: The Changeling
gmNotes:
The Changeling is one of the most nefarious and favoured Daemons of Tzeentch. A master of mimicry and deception, it delights in taking the form of other beings to enact its cruel will. Many once powerful commanders of the Astra Militarum or Planetary Governors have made disastrous decisions on the advice of what they thought was their most trusted advisors only to see the folly of their actions fully at the last moment.

Furthering the will of Tzeentch through cunning, deception, and devious means in tandem with the potential for cruel practical jokes and malicious behaviour has drawn The Changeling to the Sorcerer Massintos, and his grand schemes. However if you’d like to integrate the Changeling into the greater machinations of the Faithful Writ then you can make use of the additional Adventure Hooks for The Changeling presented here. The Changeling may choose to interject into the Dark Apostle’s grand plan, thwarting his efforts at the last minute for his own wicked amusement. Alternatively, The Changeling may wish to aide Maloquence on his path to Daemonhood in Tzeenths name, throwing in a few challenges for the aspiring Daemon Prince along the way.

Alternatively, if you’d prefer to allow Maloquence’s grandiose plans come to fruition on their own then The Changeling may simply disappear after they are finished toying with Massintos.

THE CHANGELING & THE DIVER’S BELL
As the events onboard the Diver’s Bell unfold The Changelings influence may present itself in a number of ways. From initially guiding the unfortunate Arden Voss towards the tainted Haemo-Rations to taking the form of numerous cult members to sow disinformation among their ranks.

Players looking in the darkest depths of the ship for the salt slicked, rusted dens the Cultists call home may find themselves aided by particularly knowing crew members. Delving further into the depths, Agents may easily become lost chasing false sensor readings and hindered by corrupted, ever changing map data.

Taking the guise of the ships commanding officers and crew, The Changeling can easily misdirect the response to the Cultists attempts to summon the mighty Screamer of Tzeentch. Players attempting to stop the Cult may find themselves aided by the crew’s limited security forces or fired upon by them depending on The Changelings interest in the Dark Apostles’ plans.

THE CHANGELING & THE FALLOW
In the depths of the Ostian Growth The Changeling sees great potential for the type of murderous comic mischief they are renown for. When present on Ostia the Players can expect The Changeling to take the form of lost Agri-Workers and lure the players into the path of the rampaging Possessed of The Fallow for its own amusement.

Elsewhere the Changeling can take the form of Medicae Hoban, misdirecting the Players in any attempts to assist the lone Apothecary or mimic the Master of Possession, Brother Ephilates to simply unleash hordes of rampaging Accursed Cultists against the Players, regardless of their alignment.

THE CHANGELING & BROTHER’S RUIN
Onboard the nightmare vessel Brother’s Ruin the Changeling can unleash their most devious trickery and malicious intent. Working against the Faithful Writ, the Changeling will delight in helping frustrate and delay the Dark Apostles plans, allowing Players to move through the ship with ease, misdirecting Chaos forces while in the form of Maloquence himself and even simply opening various bays, venting cultists into the cold vastness of space.

The Changeling may take on the form of many of the powerful Word Bearers Astartes of the Faithful Writ, frustrating the Players efforts to prevent Lord Maloquence’s dark plans, or turning on other members of the Writ and delighting in the panicked confusion that ensues.

If the ritual does take place successfully The Changeling may take the form of a powerful Greater Daemon, demanding Maloquence sacrifice his most favoured son, Iscarius, in order to complete the ritual and raise himself to Daemonhood.

THE CHANGELING IN OTHER ADVENTURES
Integrating the Changeling into the other Adventures presented in this PDF can add additional exciting challenges and ineffable danger for groups of either alignment.

An Imperial party may find the interference of The Changeling to their benefit as they attempt to disrupt and thwart the Faithful Writ’s plans. Alternatively, should The Changeling decide it wants to see Maloquences’ schemes come to fruition then it would make an excellent high tier Threat easily capable of interrupting the Players progress through both direct confrontation and, more likely, subtle trickery.

For Chaos aligned Players The Changeling may pose as an ideal antagonist as it attempts to interject in the Dark Apostles plans, confronting and confounding the players for its own amusement or to the benefit of the other scheming traitors within the Faithful Writ.

name: Brother Ephilates
gmNotes:
Brother Ephilates delights in all things twisted and Warp touched, constantly searching for the next curious concoction or sketching out the tortuous shape of a daemon’s wing. Tall for even a Traitor Astartes, his pale flesh coloured armour is covered in all manner of roughly welded-together talismans and blasphemous texts and wielding an ancient gnarled force stave, Ephilates is the Master of Possession for the Faithful Writ.

PLOT HOOK: MURDEROUS RAMPAGE
The curse of the Fallow is spreading to the surrounding farms. It starts with the baleful influence of Chaos turning food stores to sludge and making animals go wild, frothing at the mouth. Then grox are found dead, their leathery skins torn to shreds by vicious claws, and finally culminating in farmers going missing, their homes destroyed and witnesses butchered. Whispers of monsters, of heresy abound and the workers desperately call to the indifferent Imperial authorities for aid. Naturally, Ephilates is delighted by the rumours the Accursed Cultists are leaving in their wake as they abduct people for the alchemist’s twisted experiments, enjoying the chaos that simple fear can spread.

PLOT HOOK: THE GOOD MEDICAE
The farms of Ostia are poorly served by the Officio Medicae, and when a mysterious plague begins to tear through the region of the Fallow only a single officer is on hand to help.

Medicae Hoban, more recently used to curing groxflu and simple aches, is confounded by this new wasting plague that rots the mind but distends the muscles. He needs more samples if they hope to synthesise a vaccine, but these mindless brutes are proving difficult to control. Ephilates is immensely proud of this custom virus, designed to make the Human shape more accommodating to daemons while atrophying any mind that might fight off their malevolent influence and welcomes the challenge Medicae Hobans efforts bring.

MASTER PLAN: THE MASTER OF POSSESSIONS
Eventually, after investigating the mysterious occurrences and disappearances on the farms, and the spread of the bizarre plague, the PCs will be led to their source — the rusting hulk of the Mega-Harvester that Ephilates calls home.

Getting to Ephilates will be no easy task. The Mega-Harvester is hidden in the razor grass warren of the Fallow, and Ephilates’s new Mutants and Torments stalk through the undergrowth. This journey will be one full of horror: the setting Gilead sun casting eerie shadows in the crops, the rustling of plant stalks as unseen shapes move around the PCs, all before arriving at the creaking, rusted shape of the Mega-Harvester.

There are other dangers here as well: Ephilates has laid traps throughout the clearing surrounding the Harvester, a series of trip-wired rotting biological weapons known as Blight Grenades (Blast (6), Inflict (Poison 4)). If the characters manage to notice these traps, they can make a DN 5 Stealth (A) Test to avoid them or a DN 5 Tech (Int) Test to disarm them (but they still might want to wash their hands afterwards).

The inside of the Mega-Harvester is a nightmare — Ephilates has converted the systems meant for grain processing into one massive alchemical alembic, distilling and refining his weaponised plagues. The grain silos have been converted into cultivation tanks, where rotting matter and the nascent reforming Mutants and Torments writhe in the amniotic soup.

Far from being enraged at the intrusion upon his work, Ephilates is delighted to welcome guests. His enthusiasm could be described as quite literally infectious, as the longer the PCs listen to him excitedly babble about his work the more likely they are to contract some foul disease from his filthy workshop. They may well learn something if they can smooth talk Ephilates into giving away some elements of Maloquence’s plans or how his own work pertains to his master’s schemes. This is fairly easy, as Ephilates has no intention of letting the PCs leave: such fine specimens will be ideal for his experiments.

The walls of the main unit of the Harvester are covered in racks containing the dozens of missing farmers, writhing as they are poisoned by Ephilates’s new plague. They are being injected by a massive intravenous system, and if the PCs were successful in helping Apothecary Hoban synthesise a vaccine they can be inoculated en masse. Though cured, fleeing through the Fallow still offers them only a slim chance of survival, what with Ephilates’s traps and the wild Accursed Cultists. Still, a few do survive to return to their families, and by curing them the PCs have denied Maloquence his legion of Mutants and Torments, a loss for which Ephilates will pay dearly (if he didn’t meet his end at the hands of the PCs).

name: Brother Iscarius
gmNotes:
PLOT HOOK: EMERGENCY BROADCAST
Maloquence hasfinally decided to put his plan to wipe out the DeathGuard and their followers on Vulkaris into action, burning their souls to begin the ritual that will elevate him to daemonhood. While the Imperials are unaware of this plan, an unidentified craft powering towards a hated enemy can only spell doom and therefore needs to be boarded and cleansed. The Absolvers, Adeptus Soritas, and Navis Imperialis are all converging to see whether this is a threat, or an opportunity.

Onboard Brother Iscarius marshals the forces of the Faithful Writ in defence of any potential interceptions, ensuring any boarders are faced with wave after wave of heretical Threats to impede any attempts at preventing their grand plans.

PLOT HOOK: BOARDING ACTIONS
The inside of the craft christened by Maloquence as Brother’s Ruin is a nightmare, a twisted mirror of the light, fast attack ships used by the Imperial Navy. Fighting to the bridge is going to be a vicious slog, wading through the legions of Cultists, Chaos Space Marines, and Accursed Cultists, but it must be done. The deck plating has begun to vibrate with the unmistakable sensation of Orbital Lances warming up — whether this will trigger a war between the rival factions of Chaos, spilling out to engulf the whole system, or some more nefarious purpose, the path is now clear. You must get to the bridge and put a stop to this madness.

Brother Iscarius will attempt to hold the bridge until Maloquence begins his dark ritual, falling back only to witness the Dark Apostles glorious transformation into Daemon Prince. Should it look like the Players may triumph on the Bridge he falls back under the cover of the rampaging Accursed Cultists, determined to reach the site of the ritual.

MASTER PLAN: RUINOUS ASCENSION
This is Maloquence’s grand plan made manifest, all hinging upon the events surrounding the player characters. If they have failed to prevent all of the Writ’s other machinations, events will most likely proceed in the following fashion: Maloquence will have been tattooed with the ‘ink’ of Old Nine Eyes, the mind-melting ritual markings driven into his body by shivering serfs. Then he will stand upon the great machine wrought by Massintos (which may have been sabotaged by him or The Changeling) ready to be transformed.

The bridge is protected by a legion of Ephilates’s newly engineered mortal Cultists and finally, Iscarius will order the Orbital Lances to fire on Vulkaris. With their sacrifice the great machine will clank to life and the ritual will begin.

If Ephilates was stopped or somehow curtailed, the fight to the bridge is a much easier prospect, not having to face down a legion of the nimble and fast Accursed Cultists. Similarly, resistance on the bridge is much lighter for the same reason, as only the usual contingent of voidsmen are manning the stations, with the Astartes and security staff repelling the boarders elsewhere.

Secondly, if Verit was apprehended and Old Nine Eyes prevented from being summoned, the tattoos on Lord Maloquence’s body have been done with ordinary Bathysquid ink supplemented with Possessed blood. This mixture is potent, but nothing like the mystical secretions of Old Nine Eyes. If Lord Maloquence manages to ascend to the machine marked in this way, he still transforms, but merely into a into a gibbering Chaos Spawn (Wrath & Glory page 352).

Finally, and most importantly, is the machine. This vast assemblage of Noctilith, archeotech, and sorcery is the lynchpin of Maloquence’s scheme: if Massintos succeeded in tampering with it, the raw unfiltered power of the Warp is poured out of it, reducing everyone (including Massintos himself) to a pool of quivering jelly.

If the Noctilith was prevented from being added to the machine, it simply explodes, as detailed in Massintos’s mission. If The Changelings machinations are successful however, the machine will function as a ramshackle Warp gateway, and when activated provide a path to the planet Vulkaris below. The Death Guard, incensed at the attempted orbital ambush, will storm through and attempt to take the ship. Massintos will be left to face Maloquence’s rage as the daemon quietly makes its exit, ready to cause chaos elsewhere now that it is free of its foolish master.

Should the Players fail to prevent or interrupt the ritual then from the smoke, the towering form of the transformed Maloquence will lumber forward: twisted into a colossal blend of bone and ceramite, wired together with nerve and steel. Maloquence the Terrible, as the daemon prince becomes known, spells doom for anyone who is not a follower of the Faithful Writ and surely the Gilead System itself.
